study_identification.title: Mapping Neurophysiological Subtypes of Major Depressive Disorder Using Normative Models of the Functional Connectome

study_characteristics.study_objective: Quantify individual-level deviations in functional connectivity strength (FCS) across the lifespan in MDD using normative modeling, and identify reproducible neurophysiological MDD subtypes and their clinical relevance, including prediction of antidepressant response.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Group comparisons (t-tests, chi-square); ANCOVA for HDRS-17 vs. onset age by subtype; FDR correction; SVR (5-fold CV) within subtypes to predict 6-month HDRS change (significant in severe-deviation subtype: r=0.47, p=0.019).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Normative modeling of FCS revealed substantial individual heterogeneity in MDD; two reproducible neurophysiological subtypes emerged with opposing deviation patterns and distinct clinical features, and baseline deviations predicted treatment response in the severe-deviation subtype.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Across 1148 MDD and 1079 HC participants, 10-fold CV indicated good normative model generalizability (SMSE≈0.996±0.013; MSLL≈-0.001±0.007). A total of 72.82% (n=836) of MDD patients showed extreme FCS deviations in at least one region (positive 25.78%, n=296; negative 66.38%, n=762). Two subtypes were identified: Subtype 1 (37%, n=425) with severe deviations (positive in DMN/LIM/SUB; negative in SMN/DAN/VAN/VIS) and Subtype 2 (63%, n≈723) with moderate but converse patterns. Subtyping was intersite-reproducible (no significant site difference in subtype counts; leave-one-site-out overlap >92%). Baseline deviation maps predicted HDRS change after paroxetine in the severe-deviation subtype (r=0.47, p=0.019), with strongest positive contributions in DMN/FPN/VAN and negative in VIS.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Cross-sectional imaging (lifespan trajectories would benefit from longitudinal data); limited cognitive measures; treatment prediction subset comprised responders; small effect sizes indicate residual heterogeneity; data from Chinese centers limits generalizability; need external validation and richer genetic/environmental covariates.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: K-means clustering on individual deviation maps (optimal k=2 via quality indices); ComBat-harmonized FCS before modeling; leave-one-site-out reproducibility checks; SVR within subtypes with network-level contribution mapping.

general_notes.general_notes: Parcellation: 220 nodes; correlations thresholded at r>0.2; FCS z-standardized prior to ComBat. Deviations computed per ROI then summarized at network level (DMN, LIM, SUB, SMN, DAN, VAN, VIS, FPN). Supplement lists scanning parameters per site (Table S2) and extensive validation (different thresholds; sex/age subgroup modeling) with high cluster-index overlap (≈93–99%). Dataset primarily Chinese/Asian population; preprint available (bioRxiv: 10.1101/2023.02.13.528399).
